Cross-cohort replication: a preregistered-style case study

cross_cohort_replication.Rmd

This article is an end-to-end, fully evaluated template for asking: does a program-level biological effect found in one cohort replicate in independent cohorts? It uses a simulated three-cohort fixture so the truth is known, and it orchestrates existing exports only — no workflow-specific wrapper. The two transfer pathways are kept distinct:

  • Fixed-basis pathway — the discovery fit’s learned transform (gene panel, centering/scaling, loading effects) is applied to the query cohort via project_programs_to_cells(). freeze_preprocessing() alone is not this: it freezes decisions (gene panel, design), not the learned transform.
  • De-novo pathway — the query cohort is fit independently (here with the frozen feature panel, so the gene universe matches) and programs are aligned afterwards with match_programs(). Factor numbers and raw scores are never compared directly across fits.

Technical transportability (coverage, reconstruction) is reported separately from biological effect replication, and every abstention is counted with its denominator.

library(cellprograms)
set.seed(20261019)

Three cohorts, known truth

Two cell types (T, B), 24 donors per cohort, 400 genes. Planted structure in T cells:

Program Loadings Activity Truth
P1 genes 1-40, identical across cohorts correlated with donor outcome y in every cohort conserved biological signal
P2 genes 61-100, identical across cohorts driven by a batch covariate in cohort B only nuisance-only effect
P3 genes 121-160 active in cohort C only cohort-specific program

B cells carry one conserved program (genes 201-240) with no outcome link.

n_genes <- 400; n_d <- 24
genes <- paste0("G", seq_len(n_genes))
mk_w <- function(idx) { w <- rep(0, n_genes); w[idx] <- rnorm(length(idx)); w }
set.seed(42)
w1 <- mk_w(1:40); w2 <- mk_w(61:100); w3 <- mk_w(121:160); w4 <- mk_w(201:240)

mk_cohort <- function(name, with_p3 = FALSE, p2_batch = FALSE) {
  donors <- paste0(name, "_d", seq_len(n_d))
  z1 <- rnorm(n_d); z2 <- rnorm(n_d); z4 <- rnorm(n_d)
  batch <- sample(rep(c("b1", "b2"), each = n_d / 2))
  if (p2_batch) z2 <- 1.2 * (batch == "b2") + rnorm(n_d, sd = 0.3)
  y <- 0.7 * z1 + rnorm(n_d, sd = 0.8)          # outcome linked to P1
  YT <- tcrossprod(z1, w1) + tcrossprod(z2, w2)
  if (with_p3) YT <- YT + tcrossprod(rnorm(n_d, sd = 1.5), w3)
  YT <- YT + matrix(rnorm(n_d * n_genes, sd = 0.8), n_d, n_genes)
  YB <- tcrossprod(z4, w4) + matrix(rnorm(n_d * n_genes, sd = 0.8), n_d, n_genes)
  colnames(YT) <- colnames(YB) <- genes
  rownames(YT) <- rownames(YB) <- donors
  meta <- data.frame(observation_id = donors, cohort = name, outcome = y,
                     batch = batch, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  list(data = as_cell_program_data(list(T = YT, B = YB), sample_metadata = meta),
       meta = meta)
}
cohA <- mk_cohort("A"); cohB <- mk_cohort("B", p2_batch = TRUE)
cohC <- mk_cohort("C", with_p3 = TRUE)

The predeclared hypothesis, fixed before looking at any query cohort: the T-cell program whose activity tracks outcome in the discovery cohort replicates with the same sign as the discovery effect at p < 0.05. (A fitted program’s sign is arbitrary; canonicalization fixes it within a fit, so the rule is same-sign-as-discovery, not a fixed direction.) Everything else is descriptive.

Discovery fit (cohort A) 

fitA <- fit_celltype_programs(cohA$data, max_factors = 4, seed = 1,
                              feature_scale = "simulated")
fitA <- canonicalize_programs(fitA)
program_summary(fitA)[, c("cell_type", "n_programs", "R2")]
#>   cell_type n_programs         R2
#> 1         T          2 0.26394663
#> 2         B          1 0.07886538

Freeze the discovery decisions (feature panel, centering) for later de-novo refits, and keep the fitted object itself for fixed-basis projection:

frozen <- freeze_preprocessing(cohA$data, features = "all", center = TRUE)
frozen$digest
#> [1] "a92378907d03ffd308f4d967f75bf62bc71c8173e89c91233e00df622462a720"

Pathway 1: fixed-basis projection into cohorts B and C

The discovery programs are applied to each query cohort’s donor pseudobulks. Rows are type_donor so both cell types project in one call; the discovery preprocessing is replayed from the fit, not refit.

stack <- function(coh) {
  rbind(coh$data$pseudobulk$T, coh$data$pseudobulk$B) |>
    `rownames<-`(c(paste0("T_", coh$meta$observation_id),
                   paste0("B_", coh$meta$observation_id)))
}
project_cohort <- function(fit, coh) {
  expr <- stack(coh)
  cts <- setNames(sub("_.*", "", rownames(expr)), rownames(expr))
  project_programs_to_cells(fit, expr, cell_types = cts,
                            feature_scale = "simulated", min_coverage = 0.9)
}
projB <- project_cohort(fitA, cohB)
projC <- project_cohort(fitA, cohC)
projB$coverage[, c("cell_type", "programs", "cells", "shared_genes", "coverage")]
#>   cell_type programs cells shared_genes coverage
#> 1         T        2    24          400        1
#> 2         B        1    24          400        1

Coverage is complete (400/400 genes) — technical transportability holds by construction here; on real data this table is where ineligible type-cohorts are caught. Now the predeclared association on the projected T-cell activities:

assoc_projected <- function(proj, meta, ct = "T") {
  A <- proj$activity
  rows <- rownames(A)[startsWith(rownames(A), paste0(ct, "_"))]
  out <- vapply(colnames(A), function(p) {
    s <- A[rows, p]
    if (all(is.na(s))) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
    y <- meta$outcome[match(sub("^T_", "", rows), meta$observation_id)]
    cf <- coef(summary(lm(y ~ s)))
    c(cf["s", 1], cf["s", 4])
  }, numeric(2))
  data.frame(program = colnames(A), beta = out[1, ], p = out[2, ],
             row.names = NULL)
}
aB <- assoc_projected(projB, cohB$meta)
aC <- assoc_projected(projC, cohC$meta)
rbind(data.frame(cohort = "B", aB), data.frame(cohort = "C", aC))
#>   cohort program       beta           p
#> 1      B     T_1 -2.8684965 0.006144099
#> 2      B     T_2  0.5826891 0.739876914
#> 3      B     B_1         NA          NA
#> 4      C     T_1 -3.1295870 0.003218153
#> 5      C     T_2 -0.3099099 0.815471556
#> 6      C     B_1         NA          NA

One T-cell program shows the replicated outcome association in both query cohorts (same sign as the discovery effect, p < 0.05) — the conserved P1 signal. Which discovery program is it, and is it the planted one?

sc <- program_scores(fitA, format = "list")$T
disc_assoc <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(sc)), function(k) {
  cf <- coef(summary(lm(cohA$meta$outcome ~ sc[, k])))[2, c(1, 4)]
  c(cf[1], cf[2])
}, numeric(2))
data.frame(program = colnames(sc), beta = disc_assoc[1, ], p = disc_assoc[2, ])
#>   program        beta            p
#> 1     T_1 -0.77061789 2.472144e-05
#> 2     T_2 -0.01467328 9.472151e-01

The same discovery program carries the association in A and replicates in B and C through the fixed basis — score-level transfer plus effect replication, with the sign fixed by canonicalization within the projected frame.

Pathway 2: de-novo refit + matching

Cohort B is refit independently — same frozen feature panel, independent factors — then aligned to the discovery programs by loading-space matching:

fitB <- fit_celltype_programs(cohB$data, max_factors = 4, seed = 2,
                              preprocessing_spec = frozen)
fitB <- canonicalize_programs(fitB)
m <- match_programs(fitA, fitB, "T", method = "correlation",
                    space = "loadings", sim_threshold = 0.5)
m$matches
#>   program_a program_b    cosine
#> 1       T_1       T_1 0.9641598
#> 2       T_2       T_2 0.8973300

The matched B program’s outcome association is computed on B’s own scores (never on discovery coordinates):

scB <- program_scores(fitB, format = "list")$T
hit <- m$matches[m$matches$cosine > 0.5, , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(hit)) {
  k <- match(hit$program_b[1], colnames(scB))
  coef(summary(lm(cohB$meta$outcome ~ scB[, k])))[2, ]
}
#>     Estimate   Std. Error      t value     Pr(>|t|) 
#> -0.506379271  0.167712860 -3.019322857  0.006305575

Abstention accounting

Every program enters exactly one bucket per pathway; denominators are always shown.

disc_sign <- sign(disc_assoc[1, which.min(disc_assoc[2, ])])  # discovery effect direction
accounting <- data.frame(
  pathway = c("fixed-basis (A->B)", "fixed-basis (A->C)", "de-novo (A vs B)"),
  discovery_programs = c(ncol(fitA$scores$T), ncol(fitA$scores$T), ncol(fitA$scores$T)),
  attempted = c(sum(startsWith(colnames(projB$activity), "T_")),
                sum(startsWith(colnames(projC$activity), "T_")),
                nrow(m$matches)),
  ineligible = c(0L, 0L, ncol(fitA$scores$T) - nrow(m$matches)),
  replicated = c(sum(aB$p < 0.05 & sign(aB$beta) == disc_sign, na.rm = TRUE),
                 sum(aC$p < 0.05 & sign(aC$beta) == disc_sign, na.rm = TRUE),
                 NA_integer_),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
accounting
#>              pathway discovery_programs attempted ineligible replicated
#> 1 fixed-basis (A->B)                  2         2          0          1
#> 2 fixed-basis (A->C)                  2         2          0          1
#> 3   de-novo (A vs B)                  2         2          0         NA

And the cohort-specific truth: P3 exists only in cohort C. When C is the discovery cohort, its extra program must abstain in A and B — no projection target, no match. That is the correct outcome, not a failure:

fitC <- fit_celltype_programs(cohC$data, max_factors = 5, seed = 3,
                              feature_scale = "simulated")
fitC <- canonicalize_programs(fitC)
m_CA <- match_programs(fitC, fitA, "T", method = "correlation",
                       space = "loadings", sim_threshold = 0.5)
data.frame(discovery_C_programs = ncol(fitC$scores$T),
           matched_in_A = nrow(m_CA$matches),
           abstained = ncol(fitC$scores$T) - nrow(m_CA$matches))
#>   discovery_C_programs matched_in_A abstained
#> 1                    3            2         1

C discovers more T programs than A (it carries P3); the unmatched remainder is the abstention count. The leave-one-cohort-out gate is: conserved P1 replicates in every held-out cohort (shown above for B and C with A as discovery; the rotations B->A,C and C->A,B use the same code), and cohort-specific programs abstain rather than force a match.

Negative controls

(1) Permuted outcome. Replication must collapse when the outcome is permuted within cohort:

set.seed(99)
perm_hits <- vapply(seq_len(200), function(r) {
  meta_p <- cohB$meta
  meta_p$outcome <- sample(meta_p$outcome)   # shuffle values against fixed donor IDs
  aB_perm <- assoc_projected(projB, meta_p)
  sum(aB_perm$p < 0.05 & sign(aB_perm$beta) == disc_sign, na.rm = TRUE)
}, numeric(1))
mean(perm_hits)  # expectation under the null: ~0.05 per non-degenerate program
#> [1] 0.07

(2) Scrambled gene IDs. A query whose feature IDs do not match the reference must abstain loudly, not silently project:

bad <- cohB
colnames(bad$data$pseudobulk$T) <- paste0("X", seq_len(n_genes))
colnames(bad$data$pseudobulk$B) <- paste0("X", seq_len(n_genes))
tryCatch(project_cohort(fitA, bad),
         error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
#> [1] "\033[1m\033[22mCell type \033[34m\"T\"\033[39m: none of the fit's 400 genes are present in `expression`."

(3) Nuisance-only effect. P2 tracks batch in cohort B by construction. A technical association must not present as replicated biology: testing the batch term in cohort C (where no batch effect was planted) finds nothing.

sB <- projB$activity[paste0("T_", cohB$meta$observation_id), ]
sC <- projC$activity[paste0("T_", cohC$meta$observation_id), ]
batch_assoc <- function(S, meta) vapply(seq_len(ncol(S)), function(k) {
  s <- S[, k]
  if (all(is.na(s))) return(NA_real_)   # off-cell-type program column
  cf <- coef(summary(lm(s ~ meta$batch)))
  if ("meta$batchb2" %in% rownames(cf)) cf["meta$batchb2", 4] else NA_real_
}, numeric(1))
data.frame(program = colnames(sB),
           p_batch_B = batch_assoc(sB, cohB$meta),
           p_batch_C = batch_assoc(sC, cohC$meta))
#>   program    p_batch_B p_batch_C
#> 1     T_1 8.860339e-01 0.5783604
#> 2     T_2 7.579566e-09 0.4969985
#> 3     B_1           NA        NA

The batch-loaded program is significant in B and null in C — flagged as cohort-specific technical structure, excluded from the replication claim.

What to report, and limitations

A replication report from this workflow should state: cohorts and programs attempted/projected/matched/ineligible/nonreplicated (the accounting table); the predeclared association and replication rule; coverage and reconstruction per transfer (technical transportability); and the negative-control outcomes. Limitations: projected activities are query-set-dependent empirical-Bayes estimates (see the projection documentation); sign and scale are comparable only within a pathway, not across de-novo fits; and with 24 donors per cohort the power calculus here is illustrative, not a recommendation.
